---
title: "Bard_stats"
format: html
---

```{r}
## Load the necessary libraries
library(car)
library(ggplot2)

## Create two variables
x <- c(1,6,5,2,8,9,7,4,1,2,3,9,4)
y <- c(8,6,7,9,8,9,6,8,7,9,9,7,8)

## Test if the variances are equal
var.test(x, y)

## Create an IF statement to handle the difference between equal and unequal variances
if (var.test(x, y)$p.value < 0.05) {

## The variances are significantly different
t.test(x, y, var.equal = FALSE)
print(paste("The variances are significantly different. The p-value is", var.test(x, y)$p.value))

## Determine if the two samples are significantly different
if (t.test(x, y)$p.value < 0.05) {
print("The two samples are significantly different.")
} else {
print("The two samples are not significantly different.")
}
} else {

## The variances are not significantly different
t.test(x, y)
print(paste("The variances are not significantly different. The p-value is", var.test(x, y)$p.value))

## Determine if the two samples are significantly different
if (t.test(x, y)$p.value < 0.05) {
print("The two samples are significantly different.")
} else {
print("The two samples are not significantly different.")
}
}

# Plot the frequency distributions of x and y in the same chart
ggplot(data.frame(x, y), aes(x, fill = y)) +
  geom_histogram() +
  ggtitle("Frequency distribution of x and y") +
  facet_wrap(~y)
```
